answers.answer: In the 3-player case, the tied leaders gain no coin; the unique last player pays 1 coin. In a 2-player unequal Census, the unique leader gains 1 coin but the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “a tied lead gives no coin”; “In a 2-player game the last player never pays”.

answers.answer: No. Draw any number up to six, limited by the two free Market spaces, so at most two. Unused Followers already on the Market remain there between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Followers: “up to the allowance … limited by free Market spaces”; “Unused Market Followers remain between rounds and occupy capacity”.

answers.answer: You may fill an action gradually over multiple rounds, but cannot activate it until all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (Town Hall is the stated exception). A full activation may be saved for a later round. When eventually executed as an ordinary action, its Followers return to your bag; Technology stays on its space.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Planning and Actions: “fill an action gradually”; “An activation can be saved”; ordinary action Followers return to bag and Technology stays.

answers.answer: Players take one activated action or pass in clockwise order from Start Player, repeatedly. Passing ends your participation for the Action Phase, so you cannot act again later that round. Unused activations keep their Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Actions: “go clockwise repeatedly, taking one activated action or passing”; “Passing ends your participation”; “Unused activations … keep their Followers on the board”.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances the Farmers Track one space, and gives the good depicted at that space.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Farm House: “Put a new Farmer in your bag; advance Farmers Track one space and take its depicted good.”

answers.answer: Village recruits one of a Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader, placing the neutral recruit in your bag and advancing that profession’s track one space. Boatman gains the depicted coins (or a Citizen for the first player at the last space); Craftsman gains a Technology tile; Trader gains a Place Tile, category I on the first advance and I or II on later advances.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment: listed Boatman, Craftsman, Trader effects; “Put the chosen neutral Follower into your bag and advance its profession’s track one space”.

answers.answer: A newly recruited Craftsman’s Technology cannot help with another action during that Action Phase; it is used only after you pass. Your first Technology must replace a Farmer. Each Technology permanently fills one required Action Space, later Technology may replace any profession except Monk, never put more than one at a Place or any at a one-Follower Place, and it cannot be moved.
answers.evidence: Technology: first placed Technology must replace a Farmer; placement limits. Village recruitment: Craftsman Technology “use it only after you pass”.

answers.answer: No. The first Trader-track advance permits category I only; every later advance allows category I or II. Players may inspect the stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment: “first Traders Track advance permits category I only; every later advance allows I or II”; Setup: “Players may inspect these stacks at any time.”

answers.answer: University puts a Scholar in your bag, advances the Scholars Track and grants its depicted Development Points. Castle puts a Knight in your bag and advances the Knights Track; the fourth Knight leaves the allowance at 7, with no increase at that step, and the first player to reach that space takes its Citizen. Monastery puts a Monk in your bag with no extra track reward. Once a character track is at its last space, you cannot take the corresponding action again.
answers.evidence: Actions table, University/Castle/Monastery; Castle rewards; Character-track limits.

answers.answer: A Monk may replace any other profession for an ordinary action. A Knight or Technology cannot replace a required Monk. No substitution, including a Monk, can replace the exact profession depicted on a Beneficial Deed.
answers.evidence: Monks: “a Monk can replace any other profession. The reverse is forbidden”; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: “Substitutions … cannot replace the exact professions depicted on Deeds.”

answers.answer: One Ship or Wagon action moves the Merchant along exactly one connection to an adjacent town. You may take at most one good from that connection, choosing one if two are there. An empty connection is legal and yields no good.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: “just one connection”; “one good … choosing one if several”; “Empty Roads/Waterways are legal”.

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the town where your Merchant currently is. A town with any player’s station cannot receive another, except Orléans, where each player may build one station.
answers.evidence: Building: “Guildhall requires your Merchant in the town”; town limitation and Orléans exception.

answers.answer: Scriptorium gains 1 Development Point by moving one space on the Development Track. Moving onto or past a coin space gives its depicted coins; the first player onto/past a Citizen space takes that Citizen; reaching/passing a Development Status space immediately changes Status to its shown value.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Scriptorium; Scoring / Victory Conditions: effects for moving onto or past coin, Citizen, and Status spaces.

answers.answer: Town Hall activates with one or two eligible Followers; one action can send one or both, though the two may also be sent in separate action turns. Starting colored Followers cannot be used. Send each permanently to a free Deed space matching its exact profession; each placement earns its depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins, while Canalization gives a choice of 1 coin or 1 Development Point. The player filling a Deed’s last space takes its Citizen.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Town Hall; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds; FAQ: “You may send its two Followers in separate action turns”.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage forbids Monk recruitment during Phase 5 (the Action Phase), before the Event Phase. Other events are resolved for all players in Phase 6. Pilgrimage is the opening event: setup places it atop the Hour Glass stack.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Hour Glass and Event; Setup: “put that Pilgrimage on top”; Events: Pilgrimage restriction.

answers.answer: Harvest food is grain, cheese, or wine; wool does not qualify. Paid food goes to the Goods Market. If you cannot pay food, you owe 5 coins; if you have fewer than five, pay available coins and undergo torture for the shortfall.
answers.evidence: Events, Harvest; Torture: when unable to make required payment, pay available coins and replace each missing coin with an item.

answers.answer: A neutral Scholar drawn in Plague returns to its game-board supply and is recruitable again; its track marker does not move back. If the drawn tile is your marked starting Trader, keep it and lose no Follower that round; do not redraw.
answers.evidence: Events, Plague: neutral Follower return and no track reversal; marked starting Follower: keep it, no loss and “do not redraw”.

answers.answer: For a 3-coin debt with 1 coin available, pay that coin and replace each of the two missing coins with one eligible item (any mix): a built or unbuilt Trading Station; one random eligible Follower drawn only from your bag (marked starters are returned/redrawn until an eligible neutral is drawn); one Development Point moved left but never onto or past a coin space; a Goods Tile, Place Tile, or Technology tile. Items surrendered are removed from the game.
answers.evidence: Torture (bankruptcy): payment choices, bag-only Follower restriction, Development Point restriction, and “removed from the game”.

answers.answer: You cannot perform an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods tile, even if another part would still give a reward. It becomes available again as soon as its required tile is available, subject to normal requirements. If the common coin supply is insufficient, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: Limited supplies: unavailable-tile action prohibition, availability returning, and insufficient coin supply.

answers.answer: A tie for most built stations means nobody takes the set-aside bonus Citizen. Final goods values are grain 1, cheese 2, wine 3, wool 4, brocade 5 points each. Score built stations plus collected Citizens multiplied by final Development Status. For tied total scores, the player furthest ahead on the Development Track wins; if still tied, share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: unique most stations requirement; scoring table; tie-break rule.

answers.answer: Each player takes a board, bag, Merchant, 10 stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers. Put the starting Followers on the Market, Merchant in Orléans, one marker on the first space of each six Character Tracks and the Development Track; keep coins and unbuilt stations in front of you. Youngest player takes Start Player token.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 2 and closing sentence: personal components, placement, and youngest takes Start Player token.

answers.answer: Set both shared boards; sort neutral Followers by profession into their game-board buildings, Technology into its supply, and coins nearby. Place 13 Citizens on marked board/Deed spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for the final station award. Separate Place Tiles into categories I and II. In four players, shuffle goods and deal one face up to every eligible Road/Waterway goods space; sort remaining goods face up into the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1, 3, 5: Citizens, neutral Followers/Technology, Place stacks, and goods setup; 4-player spaces are all filled.

answers.answer: For 3 players, remove 2 neutral Farmers, Boatmen, Craftsmen, and Traders each; 3 neutral Knights, Scholars, and Monks each; remove 6 random goods; leave spaces marked 4 empty. For 2 players, remove 4 of each of the first group; 6 of each of the second group; remove 12 random goods; leave spaces marked 3 or 4 empty. Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.
answers.evidence: Fewer players table and preceding sentence: “Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.”

answers.answer: Farm House: Boatman + Craftsman. Village: Farmer + Boatman + Craftsman. University: Farmer + Craftsman + Trader. Castle: Farmer + Boatman + Trader. Monastery: Scholar + Trader.
answers.evidence: Actions table: required professions (before substitutions or Technology).

answers.answer: Ship: Farmer + Boatman + Knight. Wagon: Farmer + Trader + Knight. Guildhall: Farmer + Craftsman + Knight.
answers.evidence: Actions table: required professions (before substitutions or Technology).

answers.answer: Scriptorium requires Knight + Scholar. Town Hall accepts one or two eligible Followers; the summary defines these as neutral Followers and says starting marked Followers cannot enter it.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Scriptorium and Town Hall; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds eligibility rule.

answers.answer: Yes. For each draw you decline, you may move one Follower from an Action Space back to your Market; thus declining two draws can recover two Followers, if applicable. You cannot move a Follower directly from one Action Space to another.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Followers: “For each draw you decline” recover one to Market; direct move between Action Spaces is not permitted.

answers.answer: Yes. You may inspect the bag contents at any time, but must shuffle its contents afterward.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Followers: “You may inspect your bag at any time, but shuffle its contents afterward.”

answers.answer: Order: Hour Glass, Census, Followers, Planning, Actions, Event, Start Player. Pass Start Player to the player on your left. Planning starts simultaneously; announce completion and, if order matters, plan clockwise from Start Player. Payments and necessary order-sensitive resolution proceed clockwise from Start Player. Paid coins go to the common supply; received coins come from it.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: seven numbered phases and their order, Planning order, Event payment order and coin destinations, Start Player passage.

answers.answer: You do not score immediately. Finish the entire round in which the 18th tile is drawn, including its Event phase; scoring follows.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “Finish the entire round in which the 18th Hour Glass tile is drawn, including its event.”

answers.answer: The unique player ahead on the Farmers Track gains the Census coin, regardless of how many Farmer tiles are in bags.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Census: compare Farmers Track “regardless of how many Farmer tiles are currently in bags”; unique leader gains 1 coin.

answers.answer: Income pays coins equal to your current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Events, Income: “Gain coins equal to Development Status”; Scoring says Status determines Income.

answers.answer: With eight goods, pay 2 coins (one per complete group of 3, rounding down). Goods types do not matter because Taxes counts all goods. If short, undergo torture.
answers.evidence: Events, Taxes: count all goods; pay 1 per complete group of 3 (round down); shortfall causes torture.

answers.answer: You receive 4 coins, one per built Trading Station; the six unbuilt stations do not count.
answers.evidence: Events, Trading Day: “Gain 1 coin per built Trading Station”; Building says only built stations count.

answers.answer: Hayrick: Farmer; 1 grain from Goods Market. Cheese Factory: Farmer + Farmer; 1 cheese from Goods Market. Winery: Farmer + Trader; 1 wine from Goods Market. Wool Manufacturer: Boatman + Trader; 1 wool from Goods Market. Tailor Shop: Scholar + Trader; 1 brocade from Goods Market. A goods-producing Place cannot be used if its particular good is absent from the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table lists each cost, good, and source; following sentence bars use when its good is absent.

answers.answer: Shipping Line: Boatman, gain 1 Development Point. Brewery: Monk, gain 2 coins. Windmill: Craftsman + Craftsman, gain 2 coins and 1 Development Point. Library: Knight + Scholar, gain 2 Development Points.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table.

answers.answer: Any one Follower can activate Pharmacy. Pay 1–3 coins and advance one Development space per coin; paying two advances two spaces. Zero or four coins are outside the allowed range.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Pharmacy row.

answers.answer: Cellar: Monk + Scholar, gain 4 coins. Office: Scholar + Scholar, gain 1 coin per Trading Station you have built. Hospital: Boatman + Scholar, gain coins equal to current Development Status.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Cellar/Office/Hospital rows.

answers.answer: Horse Wagon requires Trader + Knight; move along one Road to an adjacent town and collect one good if available.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Horse Wagon row.

answers.answer: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile, subject to usual placement rules. Your first Technology cannot be placed there because it must replace a Farmer. A later Technology may go on either Laboratory space if neither already holds Technology and the usual constraints are met.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Laboratory row; Technology section, first Farmer rule and one Technology per Place limit.

answers.answer: Bathhouse requires a Farmer. Draw three Followers from your bag, choose two, and immediately place them on appropriate Action Spaces; none may go on Bathhouse. Return the third drawn Follower and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Bathhouse row.

answers.answer: If only one of the three drawn Followers can legally be placed, place that one on an appropriate Action Space; return the other two drawn Followers and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag. If none can be placed, return all three drawn Followers and the activating Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse row: “If you can legally place only one or none, do so and return all other drawn Followers to the bag”; also return activating Follower.

answers.answer: It may be executed later this round on a later action turn, provided you have not passed: actions can be chosen in any order, and passing ends your participation. The summary does not state this Bathhouse-specific timing explicitly, but its general Action Phase rules support it.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Actions: choose actions’ order freely; one activated action or pass each turn; passing ends participation.

answers.answer: Sacristy requires a Monk. If activated, it protects against negative events such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague; during Phase 6 return its Monk to your bag instead of suffering the event.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Sacristy row.

answers.answer: No. Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment in Phase 5, while Sacristy’s event protection is used in Phase 6. Its Phase 6 effect does not remove the Phase 5 recruitment prohibition.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Hour Glass: Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5; Sacristy row: protection during Phase 6.

answers.answer: Herb Garden allows Boatmen to replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions; it does not permit replacing Knights, Scholars, or Monks.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Herb Garden row.

answers.answer: School allows Scholars to replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions. It has no activation cost (“No activation”).
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, School row.

answers.answer: No. Deed placements require the exact depicted professions; substitutions, including Place abilities, cannot replace them. The same rule applies when sending Followers from Gunpowder Tower to Deeds.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: substitutions cannot replace exact Deed professions; Gunpowder Tower row says Deed spaces still require exact types.

answers.answer: Gunpowder Tower adds 2 Market spaces. During Phase 3 place 1 or 2 drawn Followers there. During Planning, move one or both to Action Spaces; alternatively, during Actions send one or both directly to Beneficial Deeds in one action. Starting marked Followers cannot be sent; Deed spaces require exact types.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Gunpowder Tower row.

answers.answer: The unique leader gains 1 coin. The two players tied furthest behind pay nothing because a tied last place pays nothing.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Census: unique leader gains; “a tied last place pays nothing.”

answers.answer: The unique player with the most built stations receives the set-aside Citizen after finishing the entire round in which the 18th tile is drawn, before scoring. It counts as a collected Citizen in the final stations-plus-Citizens scoring.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: finish the 18th-tile round; before scoring unique station leader takes Citizen; scoring formula includes collected Citizens.

answers.answer: Remove the lighter Pilgrimage tile, shuffle the other 17 Hour Glass tiles face down, then put Pilgrimage on top, so it is round 1. In Phase 1 the Start Player reveals the top tile.
answers.evidence: Setup: Hour Glass stack preparation; Turn Structure, Hour Glass: Start Player reveals the top tile.

answers.answer: Each remaining coin is worth 1 victory point.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions table: Coins — 1 each.

answers.answer: Initial Development Status is 1 and initial Knight-track draw allowance is 4.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 2: “Development Status starts at 1; initial draw allowance is 4.”

answers.answer: Only lost Development Points can be regained. Surrendered goods, Followers, stations, Places, and Technology are removed from the game rather than returned to supplies.
answers.evidence: Torture (bankruptcy): “Items surrendered to torture are removed from the game”; “Only lost Development Points can be regained.”

answers.answer: You may choose the execution order freely; it need not be printed board order or the order in which Places were filled.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Actions: “Choose your actions’ order freely.”

answers.answer: The passive ability is available immediately, including during the current Action Phase.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment, Trader: acquired Place and passive special ability “available immediately, including during the current Action Phase.”

answers.answer: You may send just one, or send both; Town Hall’s one or two spaces and one-or-both rule allow a single selected transfer even when two Followers are present.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Town Hall: “Permanently send one or both”; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: “send one or both”.

answers.answer: Taking a good is optional: you may take one, and the summary does not require you to do so. You may complete the move and leave the available good there.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: “You may take one good from that connection”.

answers.answer: Yes. You may send the two Town Hall Followers in separate action turns during the same Action Phase, before passing.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings, Town Hall in separate action turns: explicit separate-turn permission before passing.
